question: Does slope measured from orbit (HiRISE 1 m DTM) match the tilt Perseverance actually experienced on the ground?

baseline.label: No-skill guess: every waypoint = median rover tilt

method: Each unique Perseverance waypoint inside the Jezero HiRISE DTM footprint is mapped to its native 1 m pixel (planetocentric lat/lon on the 3,396,190 m sphere, equirectangular latTs=0). Native float32 samples are read by exact HTTP byte range; a least-squares plane is fitted over a disc around the position and its slope compared with the rover attitude (tilt) recorded at that waypoint in the NASA MMGIS localisation record. Rover tilt includes rocks, wheel sinkage and localisation error; the DTM resolves features of roughly 3 m and larger. Agreement classes: <10, 10-20, 20-30, >=30 degrees.

sources.credit: Perseverance localisation: NASA/JPL-Caltech (MMGIS). DTM: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona/USGS.
